metadata.note: The Louisville, Cincinnati and Lexington ('the Short Line') was formed in Sept 1869 from the Louisville and Frankfort and the Lexington and Frankfort, jointly operated since 1857. It ran Louisville - LaGrange - Frankfort - Lexington and, from 28 June 1869, the Short Line from LaGrange to Covington, extended to Cincinnati through Newport over the Newport and Cincinnati Bridge from April 1872. Receivership from 21 Sept 1874; reorganized as the LC&L Railway 1 Feb 1877; bought by the Louisville and Nashville 1 July 1881, L&N operating from 1 Nov 1881. Three features: Louisville - Lexington 1869-1881 (era alignment via LaGrange and Eminence), Short Line LaGrange - South Covington 1869-1872, Short Line Louisville - Newport - Cincinnati 1872-1881. The L&N features that follow (ln_louisville_frankfort_lexington.geojson, ln_louisville_cincinnati.geojson) were trimmed to start in 1881 in the same change. The LC&L's 1875-1880 operation of the leased Lexington - Mt. Sterling line is drawn in elizabethtown_lexington_and_big_sandy_railroad.geojson.
metadata.ownership_split: Predecessors -> LC&L at the Sept 1869 consolidation (Louisville - Lexington). The Short Line's trains of 28 June - Sept 1869 are drawn as LC&L: they were run under the LC&L-style name by the Louisville-side company that built the line. The 21 Sept 1874 receivership and the 1 Feb 1877 Railroad -> Railway reorganization are NOT splits (same trains, same management line, same colour). LC&L -> L&N in 1881 (purchase 1 July, L&N operating 1 Nov) IS a split: these features end 1881 and the L&N features start 1881.
metadata.omitted: Not drawn: the Shelby Railroad / Louisville and Shelbyville (Anchorage - Shelbyville, opened 1870) - a separate company the LC&L only connected with at Anchorage; the Kentucky Central (Covington - Paris - Lexington), separate until the L&N in 1891; the proposed Covington - Big Sandy extension (never built by the LC&L); any LC&L Covington passenger service after April 1872 (no confirmed year); the last ~2-3 mi from the South Covington junction into a Covington depot 1869-72 (unsourced, see not_yet_sourced); the ~0.95 mi from the end of traced track into the Jefferson & Brook depot at Louisville (alignment not located). The 1852-1869 predecessor years (Louisville and Frankfort / Lexington and Frankfort) remain on the L&N feature in ln_louisville_frankfort_lexington.geojson - recorded there as a finding, outside this road.
metadata.freight_only_check: No freight-only years drawn. The LC&L had no known freight-only branches; the post-1985 Latonia - Newport 'Wilder' freight remnant is L&N/CSX history and is not drawn (its track is used here only as geometry for the 1872-1881 passenger route).
metadata.horsecar_check: None: steam throughout. The predecessor Lexington & Ohio's 1830s horse traction is far outside these years.
conflicts: Consolidation date: Kentucky Gazette 15 Sept 1869 reports the articles signed Saturday 11 Sept 1869; Wikipedia's Louisville and Frankfort Railroad article says the full merger was 1867, and the July 1869 Cincinnati Enquirer already uses an LC&L-style name. Drawn split 1869 either way.
Bridge opening: 1 April 1872 (queencityhistory) vs March 1872 (NKY Tribune quoting the Covington Journal; a five-engine test crossing was in March). Year agrees.
Louisville - Covington mileage: 108 mi (contemporary press via NKY Tribune) vs ~101-103 route miles (Wikipedia LCL Subdivision). Drawn Louisville - Latonia is 103.7 mi.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Covington terminal 1869-1872: no source names the station or says whether LC&L trains ran over Kentucky Central rails from the South Covington junction into the KC's Covington depot, or how passengers crossed to Cincinnati (suspension-bridge omnibus or ferry) - the Short Line (LaGrange - Covington) feature stops at the junction. Whether any LC&L Covington service continued after April 1872 - not found either way. 1870s train frequency beyond the 1870-71 ads (two each way daily except Sunday on the Lexington line; 'both trains connect at LaGrange for Cincinnati') - every headway here is an estimate. The Frankfort times carried over from the earlier L&N layer have no recorded source. The Louisville approach from Beargrass Creek to the Jefferson & Brook depot is not located. Not checked: ICC valuation abstracts and a full 1870s Travelers' Official Guide table, which would give station lists and train counts.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced end to end, no straight-line legs: 92.6 mi drawn against ~94 mi documented (Louisville - Frankfort ~65 + Frankfort - Lexington ~29; standard figures, not individually sourced - research report). Frankfort lands at 64.0 mi on the drawn line (Anchorage 11.2, LaGrange 25.6, Eminence 38.4, Pleasureville 42.6, Bagdad 51.1, Midway 78.2), so Frankfort - Lexington is 28.6 mi. Routed on OpenHistoricalMap's "Louisville & Frankfort R. R." ways (61.1 mi) and "Lexington & Frankfort R.R." ways (29.2 mi), plus 2.3 mi of live OSM track tagged old_railway_operator=L&N at the Louisville end where OHM's L&F way begins. Cross-check: 87.5 mi of the drawn line lies within 25 m of OSM ways - live track tagged old_railway_operator=L&N 68.8 mi (CSX LCL Subdivision Louisville - LaGrange 25.1, Louisville Terminal Sub 1.6), abandoned grade tagged old_railway_operator=L&N 16.2 mi (LaGrange - Eminence - Pleasureville - Bagdad, incl. Giltner Road), untagged rail 1.8 mi, Town Branch trails in Lexington 0.7 mi - and the remaining ~5 mi is OHM only. LIFTED: LaGrange - Eminence - Pleasureville - Bagdad (about 25 mi) survives only as abandoned grade and OHM mapping (OHM end_date 1959 on the LaGrange - Pleasureville way, an OHM claim not checked here). Waypoints are OSM place nodes (Nominatim answered HTTP 429 during this session; each place node's type checked - village/town/hamlet/city - and pinned): Pewee Valley, Crestwood, Buckner, LaGrange, Eminence, Pleasureville, Cropper, Bagdad and Midway within 0.07 km of the line, Frankfort 0.29 km, Anchorage 0.43 km. LOUISVILLE END: the drawn line starts where traced track ends near Beargrass Creek (-85.7298, 38.2512), about 1.5 km (~0.95 mi) east of the Jefferson & Brook Streets depot; that last stretch into the depot is NOT drawn and its alignment is not located. LEXINGTON END: OHM L&F ways along Vine Street (formerly Water Street) to Mill Street - the Mill & Water Streets depot; two short OHM pieces there carry start_date 1887, the date of the Totten map they were digitised from, and overlap 1834-dated ways on the same line. ALIGNMENT ERA: the Louisville & Frankfort / Lexington & Frankfort alignment via LaGrange that the 1870-71 timetables describe, NOT the Anchorage - Simpsonville - Shelbyville - Christiansburg routing drawn by the L&N feature in ln_louisville_frankfort_lexington.geojson; a check against every OHM way in the corridor found no part of the line on a way dated outside 1869-1881 (in Frankfort it uses OHM's 1848 L&F way, not the 1834-1847 alignment). Louisville - LaGrange is the same track as the Short Line (Louisville - Cincinnati) feature and is drawn with identical coordinates there.
properties.documented_mileage: ~94 mi (Louisville - Frankfort ~65, Frankfort - Lexington ~29; standard figures, not individually sourced)

segments.note: Louisville, Cincinnati and Lexington Railroad, formed by consolidation articles signed Saturday 11 Sept 1869 (Kentucky Gazette 15 Sept 1869) merging the Louisville and Frankfort and the Lexington and Frankfort, which had operated jointly as the 'Louisville, Frankfort and Lexington' since 1 Jan 1857 (Wikipedia's L&F article dates the merger 1867 - conflict recorded in metadata). The 'Cincinnati' in the name came from the Short Line, which left this route at LaGrange (not 'near Anchorage', as the earlier L&N layer's note said) for Covington, opened 28 June 1869, and reached Cincinnati over the Newport and Cincinnati Bridge from April 1872 - see the two Short Line features in this file. Lexington trains ran through LaGrange, Eminence, Pleasureville and Bagdad: the Kentucky Gazette ad dated 20 Oct 1870 shows two trains each way daily except Sunday (leave Lexington 6:00 AM and 1:40 PM, arrive Louisville 11:00 AM and 6:30 PM; leave Louisville 6:00 AM and 2:50 PM), the 1:40 PM 'makes close connection at LaGrange with the Short Line cars for Cincinnati'; the ad effective 17 Dec 1871 says 'Both trains connect at LaGrange for Cincinnati' and that the 5:30 AM train connects at Anchorage for Shelbyville (a separate company's line, not drawn). Lexington ticket office and depot at Mill and Water Streets. The Frankfort times carried over from the earlier L&N layer (leave Frankfort 9:20 a.m. and 5:50 p.m. for Lexington, 7:08 a.m. and 3:33 p.m. for Louisville) have no recorded source - unverified. END 1874: receivership from 21 Sept 1874 (Wikipedia) - receivers operating, not an operator change; the era break is kept only to carry the earlier layer's eras. headway_min 480 is an ESTIMATE carried over from the earlier L&N layer; the 1870-71 ads show two trains each way daily except Sunday.
sources: Segment-level: Kentucky Gazette 15 Sept 1869 p2 for the Sept 1869 consolidation; Kentucky Gazette LC&L timetable ads (schedule of 20 Oct 1870 printed 28 Dec 1870 p1 and 4 Feb 1871 p1; schedule effective 17 Dec 1871 printed 10 Apr 1872 p1) for two trains each way via LaGrange; Wikipedia LC&L article for the 21 Sept 1874 receivership - as read for research/branches/louisville_cincinnati_and_lexington_railroad.txt. The headway is an estimate and the Frankfort times are unsourced.

segments.note: LC&L in receivership from 21 Sept 1874 until reorganized as the Louisville, Cincinnati and Lexington Railway on 1 Feb 1877 (Wikipedia LC&L article). Same trains and same management line, receivers operating - not an operator change, same colour. The earlier L&N layer assumed service was reduced during the receivership; no 1874-77 timetable has been read. headway_min 720 is an ESTIMATE carried over from that layer.
sources: Segment-level: Wikipedia LC&L article for the 21 Sept 1874 receivership and the 1 Feb 1877 reorganization (as cited in research/branches/louisville_cincinnati_and_lexington_railroad.txt). Headway NOT sourced.

segments.note: Louisville, Cincinnati and Lexington Railway, reorganized 1 Feb 1877 (Wikipedia). The Louisville and Nashville bought the company 1 July 1881 and 'began operating trains along the old Lexington & Ohio line' on 1 Nov 1881 (Lexington History Museum wiki); either way the split year is 1881, and from 1881 the line is the L&N feature in ln_louisville_frankfort_lexington.geojson. headway_min 480 is an ESTIMATE carried over from the earlier L&N layer ('assumed similar to the pre-receivership LC&L schedule'); no 1877-81 timetable has been read.
sources: Segment-level: Wikipedia LC&L article for the 1 Feb 1877 reorganization; Lexington History Museum wiki (node 583) for the L&N purchase of July 1881 and L&N operation from 1 Nov 1881 - as cited in research/branches/louisville_cincinnati_and_lexington_railroad.txt. Headway NOT sourced.

segments.note: The Short Line: LC&L trains from Louisville ran through LaGrange (where this line leaves the Lexington line) and on via Campbellsburg, Sulphur, Worthville, Walton and Verona to Covington. Opened to regular traffic 28 June 1869 (NKY Tribune); the Cincinnati Enquirer of 4 July 1869 says the road 'was opened to public travel just one week ago' and 'has been doing an immense passenger business' (reprinted New York Herald 7 July 1869; also Evansville Journal 5 July 1869). The trains began about ten weeks before the 11 Sept 1869 consolidation articles, but were run under the LC&L-style name by the Louisville-side company that built the line, so no separate operator is drawn. Louisville - Covington about 4 hours (NKY Tribune). TERMINAL - UNRESOLVED: the line ran to 'a temporary junction with the Kentucky Central Railroad in South Covington' (NKY Tribune), and queencityhistory says it was 'run through Covington' with Covington its terminus, but no source found names the Covington station, says whether LC&L trains ran the last ~2-3 miles over Kentucky Central rails to the KC's Covington depot, or says how passengers crossed to Cincinnati (Roebling suspension bridge or ferry). The line is therefore drawn only to the Kentucky Central junction at South Covington - the safe, shorter choice - and NOT across the Ohio: no rail crossing existed. Through-ticket ads of 1870-71 ('the Short Line cars for Cincinnati') ticket a Cincinnati destination, not rail into Cincinnati. END 1872: superseded when the Newport and Cincinnati Bridge opened, 1 April 1872 (queencityhistory; March 1872 per NKY Tribune quoting the Covington Journal - year agrees). Whether any LC&L Covington passenger service survived after April 1872 is not established either way, so nothing is drawn after 1872. The Louisville - LaGrange part of the run is the Louisville - Lexington feature's track and is not redrawn here. headway_min 720 is an ESTIMATE from 'Both trains connect at LaGrange for Cincinnati' (Kentucky Gazette ad, Dec 1871).
sources: Segment-level: NKY Tribune (2021) for the 28 June 1869 opening and the temporary junction with the Kentucky Central at South Covington; Cincinnati Enquirer 4 July 1869 via New York Herald 7 July 1869 p8, and Evansville Journal 5 July 1869 p1, for the opening; queencityhistory for Covington as terminus in 1869 and the 1 April 1872 bridge opening that ends this segment. The Covington station is NOT sourced; the headway is an estimate.

properties.line: Louisville, Cincinnati and Lexington: Short Line (Louisville – Cincinnati)
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE from 'Louisville - Covington 108 miles in about 4 hours' (NKY Tribune, pre-bridge) = ~43 km/h, rounded down to 40 for the extra Newport/bridge running. Not from a timetable.
properties.geometry_source: OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=L&N (CSX LCL Subdivision), the OSM Wilder Branch, abandoned railway ways on Saratoga Street and the Purple People Bridge (maps.mail.ru Overpass mirror), and OpenHistoricalMap "Louisville & Frankfort R. R." for Louisville - LaGrange, routed with opstrace.py, 2026-10-28
properties.geometry_quality: Traced end to end, no straight-line legs: 108.2 mi drawn Louisville - Cincinnati (Newport and Cincinnati Bridge north end) against ~110 mi documented (research report). Mileposts on the drawn line: LaGrange 25.6, Worthville 52.7, Walton 88.2, Latonia 103.7, Newport Saratoga St 107.0. Sources: Louisville - LaGrange 25.6 mi is identical to the Louisville - Lexington feature (OHM "Louisville & Frankfort R. R." coinciding with OSM CSX LCL Subdivision, old_railway_operator=L&N); LaGrange - Latonia on OSM live track tagged old_railway_operator=L&N (CSX LCL Subdivision about 74 mi beyond LaGrange, Cincinnati Terminal Sub 1.5 mi); the Newport line 4.2 mi from the Kentucky Central crossing at South Covington: OHM-1869 ways to the crossing, the Licking River bridge and the east bank on the OSM "Wilder Branch" (live rail, untagged operator) about 2.7 mi, then abandoned railway ways on Saratoga Street in Newport (the street follows the grade diagonally to the river) and the abandoned railway on the Purple People Bridge, 1.1 mi together, ending at the bridge's north end at Butler Street. Waypoints (OSM place nodes, types checked, pinned): all within 0.25 km except Anchorage 0.43 and Independence 1.87 km; Newport Saratoga St and the bridge's north end on the line. The Louisville end is the same as the Louisville - Lexington feature: about 1.5 km (~0.95 mi) short of the Jefferson & Brook depot, NOT drawn. CINCINNATI END: stops at the north bridgehead (Butler Street); the Little Miami depot at Butler/Pearl Streets that the LC&L backed into is adjacent but its track layout is not drawn. ALIGNMENT ERA: this is the 1872 Newport approach (Saratoga Street - Newport and Cincinnati Bridge - Little Miami terminal; jjakucyk, queencityhistory), NOT the later Covington - C&O bridge - Union Terminal (1933) approach drawn by the L&N feature in ln_louisville_cincinnati.geojson. OHM maps the Saratoga Street line and the bridge only as a 1900-1901 snapshot (start_date 1900, end_date 1901 - a map-evidence date, not a construction date); the bridge superstructure seen in OSM is the later rebuild on the same crossing (the bridge is today's Purple People Bridge). LaGrange - Latonia is the surviving CSX line; no relocation since 1872 is documented in the report's sources, but none was looked for. Licking River - Newport: the Wilder Branch is the post-1985 freight remnant of the same Latonia - Newport line (research report).

segments.note: Through LC&L Short Line trains Louisville - LaGrange - Campbellsburg - Worthville - Walton - Latonia - Newport - Cincinnati from the opening of the Newport and Cincinnati Bridge on 1 April 1872 (queencityhistory; March 1872 per NKY Tribune quoting the Covington Journal, when a five-engine test train crossed - year agrees). The LC&L laid track from Latonia north on Saratoga Street in Newport to the riverbank; the bridge (Newport and Cincinnati Bridge Co., owned with the Little Miami) connected to the Little Miami's terminal area on Butler Street, the later Pan Handle Station, where LC&L trains had to pull past the station and back in (jjakucyk). The bridge is today's Purple People Bridge; rail removed 1984-85. Through cars Cincinnati - Louisville connected for Nashville and the South. LC&L Railroad to 1 Feb 1877 (receivers from 21 Sept 1874), LC&L Railway from 1877 - not operator changes. END 1881: L&N purchase 1 July 1881, L&N operating from 1 Nov 1881 (Lexington History Museum wiki); from 1881 the route is the L&N feature in ln_louisville_cincinnati.geojson. headway_min 720 is an ESTIMATE: at least two each way daily is implied by 'Both trains connect at LaGrange for Cincinnati' (Kentucky Gazette ad, Dec 1871); 1870s frequency is otherwise uncounted.
sources: Segment-level: queencityhistory and NKY Tribune for the April (March) 1872 bridge opening; jjakucyk for the Saratoga Street route and the Little Miami / Pan Handle terminal; Kentucky Gazette 10 Apr 1872 p1 for the Dec 1871 LaGrange connection; Wikipedia LC&L article and lexhistory.org for the 1881 L&N takeover - as read for research/branches/louisville_cincinnati_and_lexington_railroad.txt. The headway is an estimate.
